units.explanation: Requires the Volunteer, upon termination of service, to return the specified Confidential Information and all copies within ten business days.

links.quote: Volunteer further agrees that no copies, electronic or otherwise, notes or abstracts of the foregoing shall be retained and that all information will be returned not destroyed.
Volunteer further agrees that no copies, electronic or otherwise, notes or abstracts of the foregoing shall be retained and that all information will be returned not destroyed.

units.explanation: Continues the termination-triggered return arrangement in unit 29, prohibits retaining copies, notes, or abstracts, and requires return rather than destruction. “The foregoing” supplies the information scope from unit 29.
Requires return of documents, materials, and copies within one month after either stated trigger, together with written certification of compliance.

links.quote: notwithstanding completion of the Purpose or return of documents and materials as aforesaid, continue to be bound by the undertakings set out in clause 2
return of documents and materials as aforesaid

units.explanation: Does not impose a disposal or retention action; it makes the clause 2 undertakings continue after the return process in unit 50. The phrase “as aforesaid” expressly refers to that earlier return.
Establishes the termination-triggered principal duty to return all Confidential Information and copies, subject to different written instructions from the disclosing entity.

links.quote: Notwithstanding the foregoing, if the Confidential Information is retained in the computer backup system of a Participating Entity, the Confidential Information will be destroyed in accordance with the regular ongoing records retention process of the Participating Entity.

units.explanation: Qualifies the immediate return duty for information remaining in a backup system and mandates its later destruction under the regular retention process. The conditional exception alone is not treated as an affirmative retention permission.

links.quote: In lieu of return, a Participating Entity may certify to the other Participating Entities in writing that all such Confidential Information, in any form whatsoever, has been destroyed.
all such Confidential Information, in any form whatsoever

units.explanation: Allows destruction with written certification as an express substitute for the return required by unit 48; “such Confidential Information” inherits the information scope of that return duty.

links.quote: Notwithstanding anything in this paragraph 6 to the contrary, a Participating Entity may retain a record copy of any Confidential Information if required to do so by applicable law.

units.explanation: Expressly permits legally required retention of a record copy and broadly overrides contrary return or destruction requirements elsewhere in paragraph 6, including units 48–50.

links.quote: such Participating Entity shall identify in writing the specific Confidential Information retained, and shall provide the affected Participating Entity or Participating Entities with a written commitment to return or destroy the retained Confidential Information upon the expiration of the retention period required by law
return or destroy the retained Confidential Information upon the expiration of the retention period required by law

units.explanation: Uses the legally required retention instance in unit 51 as its trigger, adds identification and written-commitment conditions, and provides for return or destruction after the legally required retention period expires.

Requires timely return of all copies, permits destruction instead when elected by the Discloser, requires written certification, and expressly permits retention of one copy solely for archival purposes. There are no other reviewed focus units in this source to link.
